The Agreement on Trade in Goods of CEPA (hereinafter referred to as "the Agreement") was signed on 12 December 2018 between China and Macao China. The Agreement came into effect on the date of signature and was officially implemented from 1 January 2019. The Agreement has integrated the relevant provisions in CEPA and its 10 Supplements, and enriched the content of cooperation by establishing the rules of origin for all products classified under the Mainland tariff codes, and further enhancing the level of customs clearance facilitation, so as to promote the movement of goods between the two places and to foster the continuous development of Macao manufacturing industry.

The Agreement also has a dedicated chapter for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to implement specific measures for customs clearance of goods within the Bay Area to assist Macao's business sector to integrate into the national development strategies and promote the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in a jointly basis.

The Second Agreement Concerning Amendment to the CEPA Agreement on Trade in Services eliminates the three-year substantive business operation requirement for most service sectors, providing Macao service providers with easier access to the Mainland market. Additionally, it introduces pilot initiatives in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and includes expanded liberalization measures in sectors such as high-tech, financial services, and audio-visual culture. Moreover, it grants professionals in fields like construction and engineering, accounting, medical care, and education facilitative entry conditions into the Mainland of China, empowering Macao service providers to capitalize on their professional strengths and pursue business growth opportunities in the Mainland of China. The Second Amendment Agreement came into effect on the day of signing (i.e. 10 October 2024) and will be implemented on 1 March 2025.

The Agreement Concerning Amendment to the CEPA Agreement on Trade in Services CEPA consolidates and sums up the previous liberalization measures relating to trade in services in the CEPA series. The Agreement further expands the scope of liberalization in finance, legal, accounting, construction and engineering, cultural, tourism, distribution, education and other services sectors. Furthermore, the Agreement proposes 11 liberalization measures including finance, legal, education, construction, tourism sectors S/C/N/265/Add.11 that are implemented on a pilot basis in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

On 18 December 2014, China and Macao, China signed the Agreement between the Mainland and Macao on Achieving Basic Liberalization of Trade in Services in Guangdong under the framework of CEPA. The Agreement adopts a hybrid approach of negative and positive listings in further liberalization, covering 153 services trade sub-sectors. Among all, positively listed sectors such as telecommunications and cultural services introduce 24 new liberalization measures, including the opening up of additional 84 sectors for individually owned stores. National treatment will be applied to Macao in 58 sub-sectors, including advertising, photography, convention, hotels and restaurants, tourist guides, road transport and so on. With respect to investment facilitation, Macao service suppliers in the majority of the services sub-sectors are given the same treatment as companies from the Mainland. While the Agreement came into effect on 18 December 2014, the further liberalization measures with regard to trade in services will be implemented on 1 March 2015.

On 28 November 2015, China and Macao, China signed the Agreement on Trade in Services ("the Agreement") under the framework of CEPA. On the basis of CEPA and its Supplements, as well as the Agreement between the Mainland and Macao on Achieving Basic Liberalization of Trade in Services in Guangdong ("the Guangdong Agreement"), the Agreement further enhances the liberalization of trade in services in both breadth and depth. It includes extending the implementation of liberalization measures in the Guangdong Agreement to the whole Mainland; adding 20 liberalization measures in the positive lists for cross-border services as well as cultural and telecommunication services; and reducing the non-conforming measures in the negative list to 120. The Agreement also sets out provisions for the most-favoured treatment and investment facilitation. The Agreement came into effect on 28 November 2015, and will be implemented as from 1 June 2016.

The Ecotech Agreement harmonises and updates the economic and technical cooperation activities set out in CEPA and its Supplements. Among others are chapters on deepening economic and trade cooperation areas of the "Belt and Road" Initiative, Sub-regional Cooperation and the development of Macao as a commercial and trade cooperation service platform between China and the Portuguese-speaking countries, which are the key cooperation areas between the Mainland and Macao, China. The Ecotech Agreement came into effect on the day of signing.

The Agreement concerning Amendment to the Agreement on Trade in Services of the Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (“the Amendment Agreement”) updates the commitments on liberalisation and facilitation of trade in services under the Agreement on Trade in Services notified to the WTO on 23 March 2016 (WT/REG162/N/1/Add.9 and S/C/N/264/Add.9) and implemented on 1 June 2016 so as to enhance the level of liberalisation on trade in services under the framework of CEPA. The Agreement on Trade in Goods ("the Agreement") consolidates and updates the previous commitments on liberalisation and facilitation of trade in goods in CEPA and its relevant Supplements. On top of the existing CEPA commitments on trade in goods, the Agreement enhances the provisions on rules of origin, which include introducing a general rule of origin based on value-added applicable to products not having product-specific rules of origin, and simplifying and updating the product-specific rules of origin. The Agreement adds new Chapters on Customs Procedures and Trade Facilitation, Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures and Technical Barriers to Trade to provide for relevant measures to facilitate trade and strengthen cooperation between the two sides. The Agreement also introduces trade facilitation measures in the Guangdong-Hong Kong, Macao Greater Bay Area. The Agreement came into effect on the day of signing (i.e. 14 December 2018) and was implemented on 1 January 2019.

Remarks:
Notification of the entry into force of Decision No. 1 of 2021 of the EFTA-North Macedonia Joint Committee concerning amendments to Protocol B concerning the definition of the concept of originating products and methods of administrative cooperation.

The revised rules of the Regional Convention on pan-Euro-Mediterranean preferential rules of origin (PEM Convention) introduce a new set of modernised rules of origin designed to promote trade between the Contracting Parties to the PEM Convention. The EFTA States and North Macedonia have agreed to amend and replace Protocol B to the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) concerning the definition of the concept of “originating products” and Methods of Administrative Cooperation, incorporating a dynamic link to the PEM Convention and applying the revised rules of the PEM Convention on a bilateral basis pending their adoption by the Joint Committee of the PEM Convention.

Key changes include greater flexibility in the cumulation of origin, introducing simplified, more flexible product-specific rules, as well as allowing for the issuance of electronic origin certificates. These updates aim to reduce administrative burdens, simplify trade documentation, and offer businesses more opportunities within the PEM zone.

As Protocol B are referenced in the Bilateral Agreements on Agriculture between the respective EFTA States and North Macedonia, the amendments also necessitated corresponding changes to the bilateral agricultural agreements. These revisions ensure that the updated rules of origin and related procedures are consistently applied across the FTA and the Bilateral Agricultural Agreements, maintaining coherence, and facilitating smoother trade operations between the Parties.

Notification of the entry into force of the:

• "Agreement to amend the Free Trade Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the Republic of Chile, done at Santiago on 5 December 1996", the incorporation a chapter on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures and a chapter on Technical Barriers to Trade, as well as amendments agreed upon in the Government Procurement chapter of the Agreement; and 

• "Agreement to amend, in respect of investment and trade and gender, the Free Trade Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the Republic of Chile, done at Santiago on 5 December 1996", concerning amendments agreed upon in the Investment chapter of the Agreement, as well as the incorporation of a chapter on Trade and Gender.

The first Agreement includes amendments to the existing government procurement chapter, as well as a new sanitary and phytosanitary measures chapter and a new technical barriers to trade chapter. 

The new sanitary and phytosanitary chapter provides scope for better communication and cooperation between Canada and Chile, including through the modernized bilateral Sanitary and phytosanitary Committee, to address issues that may impact trade in agricultural, fish and forestry products while maintaining the rights of Parties to take easures necessary for the protection of human, animal or plant life or health.

The new technical barriers to trade chapter builds on the World Trade Organization (WTO) TBT Agreement, which ensures that technical regulations, standards, and conformity assessment procedures such as product testing and certification do not create unnecessary obstacles to international trade. In particular, the chapter incorporates WTO TBT plus obligations that address transparency, conformity assessment procedures, joint cooperation, and the creation of a Technical Barriers to Trade Committee, to address bilateral TBT issues such as the implementation of the Chapter.

The amendments to the government procurement chapter allow for reduced time period for submitting tenders, when the tendering procedure is made by electronic means. This adjustment promotes the use of electronic platform - including by publishing notices and accepting tender documentation by electronic means - helping to speed up procurement processes and improve its overall efficiency.

The second Agreement includes amendments to the existing investment chapter and a new chapter on trade and gender. 

The new trade and gender chapter acknowledges the importance of applying a gender perspective to economic and trade issues. The chapter provides a framework for Parties to cooperate on issues related to trade and gender and commits both sides to the creation of a trade and gender committee that will, among other things, share knowledge and best practices of programs for women entrepreneurs and women led SMEs, and encourage women’s participation in national and international economies.

The amendments to the investment chapter introduce new, inclusive elements, including language that reaffirms a states' right to regulate in the public interest and a new, dedicated article on corporate social responsibility (CSR). The update also includes procedural enhancements to the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism.

In 2014, Canada and Israel agreed to modernize the Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement (CIFTA), a goods-only agreement in force since January 1, 1997. Through two phases of negotiations in 2014-2015 and 2017-2018, updates were made to four existing chapters:

• market access for goods
• rules of origin
• dispute settlement
• institutional provisions.

Nine new chapters were added that deal with new and ongoing trade elements and issues:

• e-commerce
• intellectual property
• labour
• sanitary and phytosanitary measures
• technical barriers to trade
• the environment
• trade facilitation
• trade and gender
• small- and medium-sized enterprises

AAP.CE 1 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80) 

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 1 (AAP.CE 1) establishes a trade liberalization programme that aims to eliminate the levies and other  restrictions that affect a list of products (Annexes I and II). It does not include agricultural products.

In accordance with the provisions of Article 1 of the AAP.CE 1.28, the Agreement expired on 1 May 2003.

AAP.CE 2 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 2 (AAP.CE 2) has as its purpose to promote the maximum use of the factors of production among the signatory countries and to foster their economic complementarity, based on the establishment of a reciprocal trade duty phase-out programme. The products negotiated and subject to the trade liberalization programme are listed in Annexes I and II.

AAP.CE 3 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 3 (AAP.CE 3) aims to promote economic complementarity between the two countries, for certain products in the sanitary fittings sector, by granting tariff preferences for trade in the following products: 84.61.1.01, 84.61.1.99, 84.61.8.01 and 84.61.9.99.

This Agreement ceased to have effect with the conclusion of AAP.CE 21 and AAP.CE 21.12 with the annexes containing preferences.

AAP.CE 4 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 4 (AAP.CE 4) establishes a liberalization programme which has the purpose of eliminating levies and restrictions that affect imports of the products included in Annexes I and II of the Agreement. Likewise, provisions are established regarding the origin regime (Annex III) and safeguard clauses.

As of the entry into force of AAP.CE 35 – 1 October 1996 – the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, provisions that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 35 or those which relate to matters not included in the Agreement remain in force.

AAP.CE 5 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 5 (AAP.CE 5) establishes that Mexico shall grant a 100% preference in respect of the tariff in force for third countries on imports originating in and coming from Uruguay, with the exception of the products included in Annex I. Likewise, Uruguay will apply a 100% preference in respect of the levies in force for third countries, of the imports originating in and coming from Mexico, and of the products listed in Annex III of the Agreement.

Likewise, AAP.CE 5 includes provisions relating to the origin regime (Annex V) and safeguard clauses.

AAP.CE 5 ceased to have effect on 15 July 2004 with the entry into force of AAP.CE 60.

AAP.CE 6 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 6 (AAP.CE 6) establishes a trade liberalization agreement set out in Annexes I and II, which record the preferences and other conditions agreed between the parties. In addition, the AAP.CE 6 includes provisions on the origin regime (Chapter V) and safeguard clauses (Chapter VI).

AAP.CE 7 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 7 (AAP.CE 7) establishes a trade liberalization agreement set out in Annex II and the parties intend to add to the list included in the said annex so that by 1990 it covers 50% of all capital goods of the LAIA tariff nomenclature.

This Agreement ceased to have effect on the entry into force of AAP.CE 14, on 20 December 1990.

AAP.CE 72 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 72 (AAP.CE 72) seeks to establish a free trade area among the Parties through the expansion and diversification of trade and the elimination of tariff and non tariff restrictions affecting reciprocal trade. It also seeks to establish a legal and institutional framework for cooperation and economic and physical integration that helps create an expanded economic area.

AAP.CE 72 maintains the objectives and scope of AAP.CE 59, as well as the tariff preferences and other access conditions. It also broadens the preferences for products from the industrial, textile, clothing, metalworking and vehicle sectors.

Three Understandings were signed under the trade liberalization programme: one on the deepening of bilateral tariff preferences between Brazil and Colombia in the automotive sector; another between Argentina and Colombia on the automotive sector; and a third between Argentina and Colombia on the chemical and plastic sectors.

Lastly, this Agreement provides that once all the procedures for incorporation into domestic law have been completed, AAP.CE 72 shall replace AAP.CE 59.

AAP.A25TM 44 (Article 25 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Agreement No. 44 (AAP.A25TM 44) seeks to strengthen existing trade relations between the Parties through the granting of tariff preferences (Annexes 1 and 2) and the elimination of non-tariff restrictions in bilateral trade. It aims to create and increase trading opportunities for the Parties, on a predictable, transparent and permanent basis, through cooperation, complementarity and solidarity.

The Agreement also contains annexes on the following disciplines: the regime of origin (Annex 3), sanitary and phytosanitary measures (Annex 4), technical barriers to trade (Annex 5), and the dispute settlement regime (Annex 6).

AAP.A25TM 45 (Article 25 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Agreement No. 45 (AAP.A25TM 45) provides for the granting of tariff preferences and the elimination of non-tariff restrictions, which will help to strengthen and stimulate trade flows in a manner consistent with each country's respective economic policy.

Under this Agreement, Ecuador grants Nicaragua a 100% tariff preference for imports of 90 items, while Nicaragua grants Ecuador the same preference for a total of 96 items.

The Agreement also includes provisions on, inter alia, rules of origin, safeguard clauses, technical barriers to trade, and sanitary and phytosanitary measures.

AAP.A25TM 45 (Article 25 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Agreement No. 45 (AAP.A25TM 45) provides for the granting of preferential tariff treatment between the Parties; the elimination of non-tariff barriers; the facilitation of trade in goods; the fostering of cooperation with a view to deepening relations between production sectors; and the introduction of a dispute settlement system.

Regarding tariff concessions between the Parties, Ecuador grants El Salvador preferential tariff treatment for 214 items, while El Salvador grants Ecuador preferences for 207 items.

The Agreement also contains provisions on the following disciplines: rules of origin (Annex IV.1), customs procedures and trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade, trade defence, trade cooperation, and dispute settlement.

AAP.CE 73 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 73 (AAP.CE 73) provides for the establishment of a Free Trade Zone between the Parties and recognizes its coexistence with existing international agreements.

Likewise, it incorporates the Liberalization Programme and Origin Regime set forth in AAP.CE 35 and contains provisions concerning various domains, such as trade facilitation; small and medium-sized enterprises; competition policy; intellectual property; labour; the environment; trade and gender; and transparency and anti-corruption.

AAP.CE 74 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 74 (AAP.CE 74) sets out the intention of the Parties to undertake concrete actions to strengthen reciprocal integration and step up cooperation in the economic field and in other areas agreed by the Parties.

The Parties also express their willingness and commitment to seek the full alignment of the automotive sector with MERCOSUR, based on the Treaty of Asunción and the Ouro Preto Protocol.

The commitments agreed by the Parties within the scope of this Agreement shall be incorporated through the signing of additional protocols.

AAP.CE 75 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 75 (AAP.CE 75) provides for the establishment of a Free Trade Zone between Chile and Ecuador and sets out provisions on various topics, including the following: tariff preferences, rules of origin, trade facilitation, trade defence, good regulatory practices, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade, government procurement, competition policy, regional and global value chains, trade and labour, trade and the environment, trade and gender, economic and trade cooperation, and transparency and anti-corruption.

AAP.A25TM 47 (Article 25 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Agreement No. 47 under Article 25 of the TM80 (AAP.A25TM 47) provides for the granting of preferential tariff treatment between the Parties for goods included in Annexes I and II, on which the Parties shall not adopt or maintain non-tariff restrictions.
AAP.A25TM 47 also contains provisions on the following disciplines: rules of origin, safeguards, unfair trade practices, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, customs procedures and trade facilitation.

AAP.CE 8 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 8 (AAP.CE 8) is intended to strengthen economic and trade relations between the parties. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme is established, set out in Annexes I and II, where the negotiated tariff preferences and other conditions agreed upon by the parties are recorded.

In addition, AAP.CE 8 includes provisions on origin (Chapter IV) and safeguard clauses (Chapter V).

AAP.CE 8 ceased to have effect on 1 February 2012 with the entry into force of AAP.CE 67.

AAP.CE 9 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 9 (AAP.CE 9) has as its purpose to strengthen economic and trade relations between the parties. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme is established, set out in Annexes I and II, in which the negotiated tariff preferences and other conditions agreed upon by the parties are recorded.

In addition, AAP.CE 9 contains provisions on origin (Chapter IV) and safeguard clauses (Chapter V).

As of the entry into force of AAP.CE 48, on 1 August 2000, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions relating to matters not covered by AAP.CE 48 and those that are not incompatible with it remain in force. Subsequently, AAP.CE 48 was replaced by AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59.

AAP.CE 10 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 10 (AAP.CE 10) has as its purpose to record the preferences granted between both Governments for the import of the negotiated products (Annexes I and II), and also the specific origin requirements (Annex III). 

In addition, it nullifies the preferences granted under AAP.R 7.

This Agreement ceased to have effect with the entry into force of AAP.CE 20, later superseded by AAP.CE 48, which entered into force on 1 August 2000, itself later superseded by AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59.

AAP.CE 11 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 11 (AAP.CE 11) has as its aim the strengthening of economic and trade relations between the parties. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme is established, reflected in Annexes I and II, in which the negotiated tariff preferences and other conditions agreed upon by the parties are recorded.

In addition, AAP.CE 11 contains provisions regarding origin that refer to Resolution 78 of the Committee of Representatives (Chapter IV) and safeguard clauses that refer to Resolution 70 of the same body (Chapter V).

As of the entry into force of the AAP.CE 48, on 1 August 2000, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions dealing with matters not covered by AAP.CE 48 and those that are not incompatible with it remain in force.

AAP.CE 12 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 12 (AAP.CE 12) establishes as a goal to be reached by the end of 1993, that the "common list of industrialized foodstuffs" negotiated in this Agreement, represents at least 50% of the products selected in the "domain of industrialized foodstuffs".

This Agreement ceased to have effect with the entry into force of AAP.CE 14, on 20 December 1990.

AAP.CE 13 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 13 (AAP.CE 13) establishes a trade liberalization programme through which Argentina grants Paraguay a 100% preference in respect of products stipulated in Annex I, while Paraguay grants Argentina an annual and cumulative preference of 20%, increasing to 100% in five years (Annex II).

AAP.CE 13 incorporates provisions on economic cooperation and industrial complementarity.

AAP.CE 14 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 14 (AAP.CE 14) includes the entire tariff domain of goods classified under the LAIA tariff nomenclature and has among its objectives to facilitate the creation of the necessary conditions for the establishment of a common market between Argentina and Brazil. To this end, both countries agree to eliminate, by 31 December 1994, the levies and other restrictions applied in their reciprocal trade.

AAP.CE 15 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 15 (AAP.CE 15) establishes a trade liberalization programme that will gradually lead to the total elimination of levies and other restrictions that affect the import of products originating in and coming from their respective territories. This trade liberalization programme will be given effect through percentage preferences negotiated between the parties, and preferences negotiated through industrial 
complementarity agreements.

This Agreement has been partially superseded by the AAP.CE 36. The provisions of AAP.CE 15 that are not related to the trade liberalization programme and that have not been addressed in AAP.CE 36 will remain in force.

AAP.CE 16 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 16 (AAP.CE 16) is aimed at facilitating, expanding and diversifying trade. In addition, it aims to promote reciprocal investment, to encourage entrepreneurship and to facilitate the development of projects of common interest.

This Agreement incorporates, as from 1 January 1992, the products negotiated by the signatory countries within the framework of LAIA, with due consideration for the preferences and special arrangements, in the following instruments:

(I) Partial Scope Renegotiation Agreement No. 26
(II) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 5
(III) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 16
(IV) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 21

AAP.CE 17 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 17 (AAP.CE 17) has as its objective to establish a tariff reduction programme through which, from 1 January 1992, negotiated products will be exempt from tariff restrictions, following an exemption schedule.

In addition, the signatory countries undertake not to introduce new restrictions on imports originating in the other Party.

AAP.CE 17 ceased to have effect on 1 August 1999 with the entry into force of AAP.CE 41.

AAP.CE 19 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 19 (AAP.CE 19) aims to improve economic and commercial cooperation between both countries. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme is envisaged, along with provisions regarding the origin regime and safeguard clauses.

This Agreement was partially superseded by AAP.CE 36.

In accordance with the provisions of Article 42 of AAP.CE 36, the provisions of AAP.CE 19 not related to the trade liberalization programme that have not been addressed in AAP.CE 36. will remain in force by virtue of their strictly bilateral nature.

AAP.CE 20 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 20 (AAP.CE 20) provides that the products negotiated by the signatory countries within the framework of LAIA shall be incorporated into its text as of 1 October 1992, and that they shall be included in the following instruments, with due regard for the preferences special arrangements set out in the said agreements.

(I) Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 10.
(II) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 5.
(III) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 13.
(IV) Partial Scope Agreement of a Commercial Nature No. 18.

This Agreement was superseded upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 48, on 1 August 2000, and the negotiated tariff preferences and associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. In addition, AAP.CE 48 ceased to have effect upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59, on 5 January 2005.

AAP.CE 21 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 21 (AAP.CE 21) has as its purpose to establish the basis for the growing and progressive integration of the economies of the signatory countries. For this purpose, the preferences negotiated in AAP.R 5 and in AAP.CE 3 are incorporated into AAP.CE 21.

This Agreement was superseded upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 48, on 1 August 2000, the negotiated tariff preferences and the associated regulatory aspects ceasing to have effect. In addition, AAP.CE 48 ceased to have effect upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59, on 1 April 2005.

AAP.CE 22 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 22 (AAP.CE 22) has as its purpose to establish the basis for the growing and gradual integration of the economies of the signatory countries.

To this end, they establish a liberalization programme, through which the parties agree to grant tariff preferences on a list of products and undertake to make maximum efforts to prevent the application of measures likely to impede reciprocal trade.

With regard to the origin regime, the LAIA general origin rules will be applied, as approved by Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee. In addition, where the safeguard clauses are concerned, the parties may apply the regional safeguard arrangements approved by Resolution 70 of the Committee of Representatives.

At the same time, AAP.CE 22 establishes a regional dispute resolution regime that provides for the conduct of consultations between the parties through the specific procedures established in Article 27.

AAP.CE 23 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 23 (AAP.CE 23) aims to establish an enlarged economic area across the two countries.

To this end, a tariff reduction programme is established, pursuant to which the products included therein will be totally exempt, as of 1 July 1993, from non-tariff restrictions.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the LAIA general origin rules will be applied, approved by Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee. In addition, where the safeguard clauses are concerned, the parties may apply the regional safeguards arrangements approved by Resolution 70 of the Committee of Representatives.

AAP.CE 24 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

The purpose of the Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 24 (AAP.CE 24) is to establish an expanded economic area between the two countries that allows the free circulation of goods, services and productive factors.

To this end, the Parties agree on a tariff reduction programme that will begin on 1 January 1994. Likewise, the products included in the tariff reduction programme will enjoy the total elimination of non-tariff restrictions.

With regard to the origin regime, the LAIA general origin rules will be applied, as approved by Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee. In addition, where the safeguard clauses are concerned, the parties may apply the regional safeguard arrangements approved by Resolution 70 of the Committee of Representatives.

AAP.CE 25 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 25 (AAP.CE 25) is intended to improve bilateral economic relations between the parties, and also to strengthen bilateral commercial relations on a sound basis of dynamic balance, taking into account both qualitative and quantitative aspects. 

To this end, Annexes I and II of AAP.CE 25 set out the preferences, special arrangements and other conditions agreed upon by the signatory countries for the import of negotiated products, originating in their respective territories, classified in accordance with the LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System of Designation and Codification of Goods (NALADISA). It also includes provisions relating to the origin regime and safeguard clauses, among others.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 39, on 16 August 1999, the negotiated tariff preferences and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions of this Agreement and its protocols that deal with matters not covered by AAP.CE 39 and those that are not incompatible with the Agreement remain in force.

AAP.CE 26 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 26 (AAP.CE 26) aims to improve bilateral economic relations between the Parties, and also to strengthen bilateral trade relations on a sound basis of dynamic balance, taking into account both qualitative and quantitative aspects.

To this end, Annexes I and II of AAP.CE 26 set out the preferences, special arrangements and other conditions agreed on by the signatory countries for the import of negotiated products originating in their respective territories and classified in accordance with the LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA).

It also includes provisions on the origin regime and safeguard clauses, among others.

Under the provisions of AAP.CE 26.2, the Agreement expired on 31 December 1995. The Agreement was superseded by AAP.CE 36.

AAP.CE 27 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 27 (AAP.CE 27) is intended to improve economic and trade relations between the Parties through the elimination of non-tariff restrictions and the strengthening of negotiated preferences.

To this end, a trade liberalization programme is established in Annexes I and II. In addition, where the general origin rules are concerned, application of Resolution 78 of the Committee of Representatives is stipulated, along with the adoption of Resolution 70 of the same body on safeguard clauses.

Upon the entry into force of the AAP.CE 39, on 16 August 1999, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions dealing with matters not covered by the AAP.CE 39 and those that are not incompatible with that Agreement remain in force.

AAP.CE 28 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 28 (AAP.CE 28) aims to facilitate, expand, diversify and liberalize the trade between the signatory countries, and also to promote reciprocal investments and encourage entrepreneurship among other aims.

To this end, on their reciprocal imports the parties shall grant each other tariff preference of 50% of the levies applicable to imports from third countries not members of LAIA, with a list of exceptions (Annex I).

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 59, on 1 April 2005, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the regulatory aspects associated with them ceased to have effect. However, the provisions of AAP.CE 28 that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 59 or that refer to matters not covered by that Agreement remain in force.

AAP.CE 29 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 29 (AAP.CE 29) aims to strengthen economic and trade relations between the signatory countries by eliminating non-tariff restrictions on bilateral trade and by deepening and broadening negotiated preferences, for which purpose the Parties shall establish a trade liberalization programme.

As established in AAP.CE 29.3 this Agreement was in force until 31 December 1995. It was subsequently replaced by AAP.CE 36.

AAP.CE 30 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 30 (AAP.CE 30) aims to expand, facilitate, promote and diversify trade between both countries. To this end, they established a liberalization programme under which the parties agreed to grant a tariff preference of 40% of the taxes applicable to imports from third countries. In addition, only the restrictions stipulated in the Supplementary Notes may be imposed on the imports of negotiated products.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the LAIA general origin rules shall be applied, approved by Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee. In addition, where the safeguard clauses are concerned, the parties may apply the regional safeguard arrangements approved by Resolution 70 of the Committee of Representatives.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 59, on 19 April 2005, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions of AAP.CE 30 that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 59 or that refer to matters not covered by that agreement, remain in force.

AAP.CE 31 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 31 (AAP.CE 31) sets in place a trade liberalization compact under which the parties will progressively eliminate their customs tariffs but may maintain those that are in accordance with their GATT rights and obligations.

Chapter V of the Agreement sets out the rules that will govern the classification of the origin of the goods subject to trade.

In addition, in the event of disputes between the parties, the procedures established in Chapter XIX shall apply.

AAP.CE 31 was denounced by Bolivia on 7 December 2009, with effect from 7 June 2010. Subsequently, AAP.CE 66 was signed between the parties.

AAP.CE 32 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 32 (AAP.CE 32) aims to establish, at the earliest possible stage, an expanded economic area between the two countries, allowing the free circulation of goods, services and productive factors. To this end, the Parties agreed to remove levies from reciprocal trade by 1 January 2000, in accordance with an automatic phase-out schedule.

For the purposes of classifying the origin of the negotiated products, the signatory countries adopt the General Rules of LAIA, and also the LAIA regional safeguard arrangements.

Where the settlement of disputes is concerned, the countries will abide by the procedures established in Article 32 of AAP.CE 32.

This Agreement ceased to have effect upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 65, on 25 January 2010.

AAP.CE 33 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 33 (AAP.CE 33) creates a trade liberalization agreement between the signatory countries, with the objective of stimulating the expansion and diversification of trade between the parties, and also eliminating trade barriers and facilitating the circulation of goods and services, among other aims.

To this end, a trade liberalization programme is established. AAP.CE 33 comprises 23 chapters with provisions on the automotive sector and the agricultural sector and measures on animal and plant health, along with an origin regime and safeguard clauses, among others.

It should be noted that Venezuela formally submitted an application to denounce AAP.CE 33, on 25 May 2006, which took effect 180 days after the notification of the signatory parties and the LAIA General Secretariat, in accordance with the provision of Article 23-08 of the Agreement, that deadline being reached on 19 November 2006.

Parties concerned: Argentina, Bolivia, Plurinational State of, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay
Remarks:
AAP.CE 34 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 34 (AAP.CE 34) has as its objective the multilateralization of the preferences pursuant upon AAP.CE 15, 19, 26 and 29, with a view to the formation, at a later stage, of a free trade area, within a period of 10 years.

This Agreement was in force until 28 February 1997, the date on which AAP.CE 36 came into force.

AAP.CE 35 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 35 (AAP.CE 35) aims to set in place a legal and institutional framework for cooperation and economic and physical integration conducive to the creation of an enlarged economic area to facilitate the free movement of goods and services and full use of productive factors.

In addition, it is intended to form a free trade area between the Parties within a maximum period of 10 years, through the expansion and diversification of trade and the elimination of tariff and non-tariff restrictions that affect reciprocal trade. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme detailed in Title 2 of AAP.CE 35, Articles 2–12, is established.

Likewise, AAP.CE 35 contains provisions in the following domains: origin regime, unfair trade practices, defence of competition and of the consumer, settlement of disputes and customs valuation, among others.

Parties concerned: Argentina, Bolivia, Plurinational State of, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay
Remarks:
AAP.CE 36 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 36 (AAP.CE 36) sets in place a legal and institutional framework for economic and physical cooperation and integration conducive to the creation of an enlarged economic area that will facilitate the free movement of goods and services and the full use of productive factors.

In addition, it is intended to form a free trade area between the contracting parties within a maximum period of 10 years, through the expansion and diversification of trade and the elimination of tariff and non-tariff restrictions that affect reciprocal trade. For this purpose, a trade liberalization programme detailed in Title 2 of AAP.CE 36, Articles 2-11, is established.

Likewise, AAP.CE 36 contains provisions in the following domains: origin regime, unfair trade practices and practices restricting competition, export incentives, settlements of disputes and customs valuation, among others.

AAP.CE 38 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 38 (AAP.CE 38) aims to establish, at the earliest possible stage, an enlarged economic area between the signatory countries, allowing the free circulation of goods and services and facilitating the full use of productive factors. To this end, the parties agree to liberalize their reciprocal trade through a tariff reduction programme.

In addition, AAP.CE 38 includes provisions on origin (Annex 3) and safeguard clauses (Annex 4), together with chapters related to, among other issues, unfair trade practices, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, cooperation, etc.

Parties concerned: Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 39 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 39 (AAP.CE 39) provides that the signatory parties shall agree to establish fixed preference margins, as a first step towards the creation of a free trade area between the Andean Community and MERCOSUR.

In various annexes, the tariff preferences and other agreed conditions for the import of negotiated products originating in the respective territories of the parties are registered, classified in accordance with the 1993 LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA 1993) (Annexes I – Preferences granted by the Andean Community; Annex II – Preferences granted by Brazil; and Annex III – Preferences that Ecuador receives from and grants to Brazil, in the products on its Special List).

Where the origin regime is concerned, the general origin rules established in Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee shall apply and the specific origin requirements are set out in Annex IV.

In addition, AAP.CE 39 includes provisions on anti-dumping and compensation measures, safeguard clauses and the settlement of disputes, among others.

This Agreement ceased to have effect with the entry into force of AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59, on 1 February 2005, between Brazil and Colombia; on 1 April 2005 between Brazil and Ecuador; on 1 February 2005, between Brazil and Venezuela; and on 2 January 2006, between Brazil and Peru. However, the provisions of this Agreement that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 58 and with AAP.CE 59, when they refer to matters not covered by these agreements, remain in force.

AAP.CE 40 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 40 (AAP.CE 40) aims to facilitate, expand, diversify and promote trade between the parties and all operations associated with such trade. It is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions applied by the parties to the import of negotiated products, when they originate from their respective territories.

In addition, it incorporates an origin regime (Annex III), and also provisions relating to safeguards, unfair trade practices (subsidies and dumping), technical standardization, cooperation and other domains.

AAP.CE 41 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Economic Complementary Scope Agreement No. 41 (AAP.CE 41) sets in place a
trade liberalization compact, under which the parties agree to eliminate all customs duties on goods originating from their territories, with a list of exceptions and goods subject to a duties phase-out schedule. 

In addition, it incorporates an origin regime (Chapter IV), and also provisions on safeguard clauses, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical standardization, cooperation and other domains.

AAP.CE 42 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 42 (AAP.CE 42) has among other objectives to facilitate, expand, diversify and promote the trade of goods between the parties. To this end, the parties agree to grant each other preferences on the levies in force for third countries (Annexes I in favour of Chile and Annex II in favour of Cuba).

At the same time, AAP.CE 42 includes provisions on: non-tariff restrictions, origin regime, safeguard clauses, technical rules and regulations, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, commercial cooperation and others.

AAP.CE 43 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 43 (AAP.CE 43) has as its objective to promote the growing trade between the signatory countries in a dynamic and balanced manner and, taking into account their respective levels of economic development, the granting of concessions that will allow them to strengthen and invigorate trade flows and achieve the widest qualitative diversification of trade.

To this end, the Parties agree to grant each other preferences on the levies in force for third countries (Annexes I and II).

At the same time, AAP.CE 43 contains provisions on the origin regime and safeguard clauses.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 62, on 2 July 2007, between the parties, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions and their Protocols that are not incompatible with the AAP.CE 62, when they relate to 
matters not covered by the Agreement, remain in force.

AAP.CE 44 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 44 (AAP.CE 44) aims to strengthen and improve trade flows between countries, promoting the inclusion of basic and manufactured products in that trade.

To this end, the Parties agreed to grant each other preferences, special arrangements and special conditions for the import of negotiated products (Annexes I and II), originating in their respective territories, classified in accordance with the LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA).

At the same time, AAP.CE 44 includes provisions on the origin regime and safeguard clauses.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 62, on 3 September 2008, between Cuba and Uruguay, the tariff preferences negotiated in the Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 62, when they refer to matters not covered by the Agreement, remain in force.

AAP.CE 45 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 45 (AAP.CE 45) has as its objective to promote the trade of the signatory countries at the highest level, through the reduction or elimination of levies and other restrictions imposed on the import of negotiated products.

To this end, the Parties agreed to grant preferences, special arrangements and special conditions for the import of negotiated products (Annexes I and II), originating in their respective territories, classified in accordance with the LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA).

At the same time, AAP.CE 45 contains provisions on the origin regime and safeguard clauses.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 62, on 2 July 2007, between Argentina and Cuba, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 62, when they refer to matters not covered by the Agreement, remain in force.

AAP.CE 46 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 46 (AAP.CE 46) has among other objectives the strengthening of reciprocal trade through the granting of tariff and non-tariff preferences.

AAP.CE 46 is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions imposed by the Parties on the import of the products negotiated in that Agreement, when these originate in and come from their respective territories, registered in Annexes I and II.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the parties decide to adopt the general origin arrangements of the Association, the revised and consolidated text of which was approved by Resolution 252 of the LAIA Committee of Representatives.

In addition, AAP.CE 46 includes provisions on safeguards, unfair foreign trade practices, technical standardization and other issues.

AAP.CE 47 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 47 (AAP.CE 47) has among other objectives the strengthening of reciprocal trade through the granting of tariff and non-tariff preferences.

AAP.CE 47 is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions imposed by the parties on the import of the products negotiated in the Agreement, when these originate from their respective territories, registered in the Annexes I and II.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the parties decide to adopt the Association's general origin arrangements, the revised and consolidated text of which was approved by Resolution 252 of the LAIA Committee of Representatives.

In addition, AAP.CE 47 contains provisions on safeguards, unfair foreign trade practices, technical standardization and other issues.

Parties concerned: Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 48 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 48 (AAP.CE 48) stipulates that the signatory parties shall agree to establish fixed preference margins, as a first step towards creation of a free trade area between the Andean Community and MERCOSUR. To this end, the parties agree on a trade liberalization programme, detailed in Annexes I–III, under which the parties shall grant one another tariff preferences.

Where the general origin regime is concerned, that applicable to LAIA is adopted (Resolution 78 of the Representatives Committee), with the addition of specific origin requirements (Annex IV). In addition, the parties adopt Resolution 70 of the Committee of Representatives on safeguard clauses. As the same time, Annex V contains provisions on the settlement of disputes.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 58 and AAP.CE 59, which took place between Argentina and Colombia on 1 February 2005, between Argentina and Ecuador on 1 April 2005, between Argentina and Venezuela on 5 January 2005 and between Argentina and Peru on 2 January 2006, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 58 and with AAP.CE 59, when they relate to matters not covered by those Agreements, remain in force.

AAP.CE 49 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 49 (AAP.CE 49) has among other objectives the boosting of reciprocal trade through the granting of tariff and non-tariff preferences.

AAP.CE 49 is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions imposed by the parties on the import of the products negotiated in that Agreement, when these originate in and come from their respective territories, registered in Annexes I and II.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the parties decide to adopt the Association's general origin arrangements, the revised and consolidated text of which was approved by Resolution 252 of the LAIA Committee of Representatives.

In addition, AAP.CE 49 contains provisions on safeguards, external trade practices, technical standards and other issues.

This Agreement voids and replaces AAP.A25TM 33.

AAP.CE 50 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 50 (AAP.CE 50) has as objectives, among others, to facilitate, expand, strengthen and promote trade between the parties and all the operations associated with such trade.

AAP.CE 50 is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions imposed by the Parties on the import of the products negotiated in that Agreement, when these originate in and come from their respective territories, registered in Annexes I and II.

Where the origin regime is concerned, the parties decide to adopt the Association's general origin arrangements, the revised and consolidated text of which was approved by Resolution 252 of the LAIA Committee of Representatives.

In addition, the AAP.CE 50 contains provisions on safeguards, unfair foreign trade practices, technical standards and other issues.

AAP.CE 51 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 51 (AAP.CE 51) has. among other objectives, to promote and diversify the trade between the two countries, at the highest possible level, through the reduction or elimination of the levies and other restrictions applicable to the import of products.

AAP.CE 51 is based on the granting of preferences relating to the levies and other restrictions imposed by the parties to the import of the products negotiated in the Agreements, when these originate in and come from their respective territories, registered in Annexes I and II.

Where the origin regime in concerned, the parties decide to adopt the Association's general origin arrangements, the revised and consolidated text of which was approved by Resolution 252 of the LAIA Committee of Representatives.

In addition, AAP.CE 51 includes provisions on safeguards, unfair foreign trade practices, and technical standards, among other issues.

AAP.CE 52 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 52 (AAP.CE 52) has, among other objectives, the strengthening of trade through the granting of tariff preferences and the elimination or reduction of non-tariff restrictions between the parties.

To this end, the Parties agreed to grant each other preferences, special arrangements and special conditions for the import of the negotiated products (Annexes I and II), originating in their respective territories.

At the same time, AAP.CE 52 contains provisions on the origin rules (adoption of Resolution 78 of the Committee of Representatives) and on safeguard clauses, among others.

Upon the entry into force of AAP.CE 62, on 24 February 2009, the tariff preferences negotiated in this Agreement and the associated regulatory aspects ceased to have effect. However, the provisions that are not incompatible with AAP.CE 62, when they refer to matters not covered by that Agreement, remain in force.

AAP.CE 53 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 53 (AAP.CE 53) aims to establish rules and disciplines for economic and trade relations between the parties, within the framework of the Montevideo Treaty of 1980.

It also promotes the development and diversification of trade flows, with the aim of deepening economic complementarity and stimulating investment flows, with a view to promoting the intensive use of markets and the competitive capacity of the parties.

To this end, the parties shall grant each other tariff preferences set out in Annexes I and II. In addition, a detailed origin regime and customs procedures for the control and verification of the origin of goods shall be drawn up (Chapter IV), together with other regulations on safeguards, unfair trade practices, economic cooperation, technical standards, technical regulations and procedures for the assessment of conformity, sanitary and phytosanitary measures and other measures.

AAP.CE 54 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 54 (AAP.CE 54) is a framework agreement for the creation of a free trade area between the States parties of MERCOSUR and the United Mexican States and has the purpose of establishing a legal framework that provides security and transparency to the economic agents of the Parties, and also establishes a regulatory framework to promote and encourage reciprocal investments.

Agreements already concluded or to be concluded by the United Mexican States with each of the States parties of MERCOSUR within the framework of the 1980 Montevideo Treaty and the automotive sector Agreement between MERCOSUR and the United Mexican States; and their respective annexes shall all form part of AP.CE 54.

AAP.CE 55 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 55 (AAP.CE 55) lays the foundations for the establishment of free trade in the automotive sector and the promotion of the integration and productive complementation of its automotive sectors. The provisions set out in AAP.CE 55 shall apply to the reciprocal trade in negotiated assets provided that they are new goods. It will cover vehicles itemized in the LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA), listed in Annex I.

At the same time, AAP.CE 55 includes four appendices with bilateral provisions: appendix I (Argentina–Mexico), appendix II (Brazil–Mexico), appendix III (Paraguay–Mexico) and appendix IV (Uruguay–Mexico)., together with an origin regime (Annex II).

Parties concerned: Argentina, Bolivia, Plurinational State of, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 56 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 56 (AAP.CE 56) has the objective of creating a free trade area between the parties, whose negotiation must be concluded before 31 December 2003, through tariff reduction and the elimination of restrictions and other obstacles that affect reciprocal trade, in order to achieve the expansion and diversification of trade.

The agreements signed between member countries of the Andean Community and the States parties of MERCOSUR, within the framework of the Montevideo Treaty 1980, will form part of AAP.CE 56 and will have their validity extended until 31 December 2003. Where Bolivia is concerned, AAP.CE 36 shall be in force.

This is a framework agreement, by means of which parties signed AAP.CE 58 and 59.

AAP.CE 57 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 57 (AAP.CE 57) establishes conditions for bilateral trade between Argentina and Uruguay in products of the automotive sector, which will remain in force until the MERCOSUR automotive policy agreement is implemented.

AAP.CE 58 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 58 (AAP.CE 58) has, among other objectives, to establish a legal and institutional framework for cooperation and economic and physical integration conducive to the creation of an expanded economic area that will facilitate the free circulation of goods and services and the full use of productive factors, under conditions of competition between the signatory parties.

To this end, the signatory parties will form a free trade area through a trade liberalization programme which will be applied to products originating in and coming from their respective territories. This programme shall consist of progressive and automatic reductions applicable to the levies in force for imports from third countries in each signatory country at the time of the application of the preferences in accordance with the provisions of its law.

In addition, AAP.CE 58 includes specific provisions on the origin regime (Annex V); safeguard clauses (Annex VI); settlement of disputes (Annex VII); system of rules, technical regulations and the conformity assessment (Annex VIII); system of sanitary and phytosanitary measures (Annex IX); and system of special measures (Annex X).

Parties concerned: Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 59 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 59 (AAP.CE 59) has among its objectives to set in place a legal and institutional framework of cooperation and economic and physical integration conducive to the creation of an expanded economic area. To this end, the signatory parties will form a free trade area through a trade liberalization programme, to be applied to products originating in and coming from their respective territories, which will consist of progressive and automatic reductions applicable to the levies in force for imports from third countries.

In addition, AAP.CE 59 includes specific provisions on the origin regime (Annex IV); the system of safeguard clauses (Annex V); the system for interim dispute settlement (Annex VI); the system of rules, technical regulations and the conformity assessment (Annex VII); the system of sanitary and phytosanitary measures (Annex VIII); and the system of special measures (Annex IX).

This Agreement incorporates the preferential tariff preferences negotiated previously between the signatory parties in the partial scope agreements concluded under LAIA, in the manner reflected in the trade liberalization programme.

In addition, this Agreement incorporates the tariff preferences and other access conditions previously negotiated in the regional scope agreements concluded under LAIA, in the manner reflected in the trade liberalization programme. However, the tariff preferences and other conditions of access that are being applied by the signatory parties on the date of signature of this Agreement, under the regional agreement relating to the regional tariff preferences and the regional agreements on the opening of markets in favour of economically less developed countries, to the extent that the said preferences and other conditions of access are more favourable than those established in this Agreement.

However, the provisions of the partial scope agreements and the regional scope agreements shall remain in force when they relate to matters not included in this Agreement.

AAP.CE 60 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 60 (AAP.CE 60) has among its objectives the establishment of a trade liberalization compact between the Parties.

Where its structure is concerned, the AAP.CE 60 has 20 chapters and regulates the following aspects, among others: Initial provisions, general definitions, access to markets, the origin regime and customs procedures for the management of the origin of goods, safeguard clauses, unfair practices, settlement of disputes, transparency, administration of the agreement, exceptions and final provisions.

Under the chapter on the access of goods to the market, the parties undertake not to increase any existing customs tariff, or adopt any new customs tariff, on originating goods subject to the tariff phase-out programme. In addition, the parties will eliminate their customs tariffs on originating goods in accordance with the provisions of the tariff phase out programme.

Parties concerned: Colombia, Mexico, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 61 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 61 (AAP.CE 61) aims to lay the groundwork for the establishment of free trade in the automotive sector and to promote the integration and productive complementarity of this sector and the sectors manufacturing televisions, fertilizers and disposable razors.

Each party undertakes to reduce its import taxes on automotive goods originating in the other party, which are classified under tariff headings 87.03 and 87.04 (except those with a gross vehicle weight greater than 8.8 tonnes) according to an established schedule.

Where the origin regime and settlement of conflicts are considered, the provisions set out in AAP.CE 33 are adopted.

This AAP.CE 61 was in effect from 1 January to 31 December 2005.

AAP.CE 62 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 62 (AAP.CE 62) has as its objective the promotion of trade between the signatory parties, through the reduction or elimination of the levies and other restrictions imposed on the import of the negotiated products.

Where its structure is concerned, the AAP.CE 62 is divided into 19 chapters which regulate the following aspects: trade liberalization (Annexes I, II and III), origin regime (Annexes IV), customs valuation, safeguard clauses (Annex V), anti-dumping and compensatory measures, technical barriers to trade (Annex VI), sanitary and phytosanitary measures (Annex VII), settlement of disputes (Annex VIII), and the promotion and exchange of trade information, among others.

AAP.CE 63 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 63 (AAP.CE 63) provides that the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela shall grant a total tariff reduction and effective access for exportable products of the Eastern Republic of Uruguay, identified in the attached list.

AAP.CE 64 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 64 (AAP.CE 64) establishes that the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela shall grant a total tariff reduction and effective access for exportable products of the Republic of Paraguay, identified in the attached list, which forms part of this Agreement.

AAP.CE 65 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 65 (AAP.CE 65) incorporates a new Economic Complementarity Agreement, nullifying AAP.CE 32, and maintains the lists of exceptions set out in the 2007 LAIA tariff nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NALADISA 2007).

AAP.CE 66 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 66 (AAP.CE 66) has as its objective stimulating the expansion and diversification of trade; eliminating barriers to trade and facilitating the movement of goods; promoting conditions of fair competition in trade; and establishing guidelines for further cooperation between the parties, among other aims.

Where its structure is concerned, AAP.CE 66 is divided into 6 parts and comprises 14 chapters, which regulate the following aspects: definitions; national treatment and access of goods to the market; agricultural sector and sanitary and phytosanitary measures; origin regime; customs procedures; global safeguard clauses; unfair international trade practices; standardization measures; transparency; administration of the agreement; settlement of disputes; exceptions and final provisions.

The chapter on access of goods to the market includes provisions on the elimination of all customs duties on originating goods (with the exception of meat and variety meats, dairy products, coffee products, cereals, flours, certain seeds, oils, sugars, cocoa preparations, fruit preparations, beverages, food industry residues, tobacco products, organic chemicals), and provisions are introduced on such issues as restrictions on customs duty drawbacks on exported products, programmes to defer or suspend customs duty payments, customs valuation, temporary importation of goods and duty-free import of samples of no commercial value.

AAP.CE 67 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 67 (AAP.CE 67) has as its objectives to stimulate the expansion and diversification of trade; to eliminate barriers to trade and facilitate the movement of goods; to promote conditions of fair competition in trade; and to establish guidelines for further cooperation between the parties, among others.

Where its structure is concerned, AAP.CE 67 has 19 chapters and regulates the following matters: initial provisions, general definitions, market access, the origin regime and procedures related to origin, mutual recognition of appellations of origin, safeguard clauses, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade, unfair practices, cross-border trade in services, investment, financial services, entry and temporary stay of business persons, mutual recognition of study certificates and academic degrees, settlement of disputes, transparency, administration of the agreement, exceptions and final provisions.

Pursuant to the chapter on the market access of goods, the parties undertake not to increase any existing customs tariff, or to adopt any new customs tariff, on originating goods subject to the tariff phase-out programme. In addition, the parties shall eliminate their customs tariffs on originating goods in accordance with the provisions of the tariff phase-out programme set out in the Annex to Article 3.4-A.

AAP.CE 68 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 68 (AAP.CE 68), between Argentina and Venezuela, provides that the Parties shall grant each other a total tariff reduction on their imports, as of 1 January 2013 and 1 January 2014 respectively.

Both countries shall exempt the sugar and automotive sectors from this Agreement. In addition, Venezuela shall exempt certain products listed in Annexes I–IV for which it undertakes to grant the agreed level of tariff preferences and shall establish tariff phase out schedules.

AAP.CE 69 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 69 (AAP.CE 69), between Brazil and Venezuela, provides that the parties shall grant each other a total tariff reduction on their imports, with immediate effect in the case of Brazil and as of 1 January 2014 in the case of Venezuela.

Both countries exempt the automotive sector from the Agreement. In addition, Venezuela exempts certain products listed the Annex I for which it undertakes to grant the agreed level of tariff preferences and shall establish tariff phase-out schedules.

Parties concerned: Bolivia, Plurinational State of, Cuba, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
Remarks:
AAP.CE 70 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 70 (AAP.CE 70) sets in place the necessary conditions for the implementation of the economic space of the Bolivarian Alternative for the Peoples of Our America – Peoples' Trade Agreement (ECOALBA-TCP).

AAP.CE 70 includes, among others, a Chapter II on stimulating the growth of trade, Chapter III on productive complementation, Chapter IV on convergence, Chapter V on cooperation arrangements, Chapter VI on administration of the Agreement, Chapter VII on adhesion, Chapter VIII on the settlement of disputes, and Chapter IX on validity and denunciation.

Where liberalization of the trade in goods is concerned, it is expected that, within a maximum period of two years from its entry into force, the signatory countries that have not yet liberalized their reciprocal trade across the entire tariff domain, should establish the respective tariff phase-out schedules. In addition, the countries agreed that, during the referred period and while the commitments that will govern trade between the signatory countries to the ALBA-TCP agreement are established, they shall form part of AAP.CE 70, AAP.CE 40 signed between Cuba and Venezuela, AAP.CE 47 signed between Bolivia and Cuba, and the agreement on trade between the peoples and on productive complementarity signed between Bolivia and Venezuela.

AAP.CE 71 (Articles 7 and 8 of the TM80)

Partial Scope Economic Complementarity Agreement No. 71 (AAP.CE 71) includes chapters on market access, origin, safeguards, commercial defence, sanitary and phytosanitary regulations, trade cooperation and the settlement of disputes.
 
In the area of tariffs, Cuba grants Panama preferences for 261 items of its national nomenclature, of which 221 are at the level of 100%. Likewise, Panama grants Cuba preferences for 509 items of its national nomenclature, of which 427 items are at the 100% level.
